Hi, i'll post some stuff from attempting to compile LibBitcoin repo libbitcoin, branch version3, commit 55f0c59421b43bb8c756431da53a28daf95dd0fa (= latest).

./autogen.sh - works

CC=/usr/local/bin/egcc \
CXX=/usr/local/bin/eg++ \
CFLAGS="-Og -g -fstack-protector-all" \
CXXFLAGS="-std=c++11 -Og -g -fstack-protector-all" \
PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$LIBBITCOIN_BUILD/lib/pkgconfig" \
./configure --prefix=$LIBBITCOIN_BUILD \
            --exec-prefix=$LIBBITCOIN_BUILD \
            --with-icu \
            --with-png \
            --with-qrencode  

- works.

gmake -j1 V=1        - on this OpenBSD 6.2 with GCC 4.9.4 (as egcc/eg++), the compilation failed with std:align not being implemented.

talking to people deep in the Gnu GCC/LibBoost toolchain, they highlighted that adding " -DBOOST_NO_CXX11_STD_ALIGN" to CXXFLAGS would trig Boost's mitigation for GCC versions below 5.1.0, to not use std:align when in C++11x, as std:align was implemented first in GCC 5.1.0.

So did some more learning over here.

OpenBSD 6.2's Boost port which is Boost 1.58.0, was built using GCC 4.2.1.

OpenBSD 6.3's Boost port which is Boost 1.66.0, is built using GCC 4.9.4.

this was effectuated by the older port's Makefile not having any COMPILER line, whereas the new one has a COMPILER line which contains "ports-gcc", <https://man.openbsd.org/bsd.port.mk#COMPILER> .

by the way, a curious thing about Boost 1.58.0 on OpenBSD:

the 1.58.0 port specified a special user.hpp file (found here:
https://cvsweb.openbsd.org/cgi-bin/cvsweb/ports/devel/boost/files/Attic/user.hpp?rev=1.6&content-type=text/x-cvsweb-markup
does specify that there are some incompatibilities between language standards, even if indeed they are rare.
It cannot hurt to use the correct compiler.
